speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I understand you are experiencing wrist pain and difficulty moving your hand; please describe exactly where the pain is located and what specific movements make it worse. To better assess your injury, would you mind telling me how this started and if you have noticed any swelling or bruising?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: The radiation of pain from your right thumb to your elbow, combined with worsening symptoms during gripping, strongly suggests pathology involving the median nerve or the first carpometacarpal joint. Given your history of a fall six months ago, did you experience any instability or clicking in that wrist at the time, or was there immediate significant swelling? REQUEST TEST: X-Ray right wrist and elbow.
